history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration improve the formulation of resource requirements for multi-year capital construction budgets based on actual project implementation and revised project schedules in order to limit the unspent balances of the projects at the end of each budget period.
history.administration_response: The United Nations Office at Geneva continues to improve its forecasting for resource requirements for its multi-year construction budget. As programme management costs are relatively fixed, the main variable is the contractor’s cash flow forecast. The strategic heritage plan team is working closely with the contractor to obtain accurate scheduling and costing data. If resource needs change, the project team informs United Nations Headquarters as soon as possible (as the Office did in December 2022) to limit unspent balances at the end of the budget period. The strategic heritage plan team notes, however, that those balances are carried over and deducted from the following year’s assessment.
history.board_assessment: Given that the cash balance of 64CFA remains high, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.sg_progress: The Administration continues to align the projected resource requirements for the upcoming period with both the most recent project schedule and the revised cost plan, while fully taking into account the projected unused balance at the end of the current period, and only the net requirement is being requested in the annual progress reports of major construction projects. The updated project implementation, project schedules and status of appropriation for the United Nations Office at Nairobi’s office blocks A to J project will be presented in the report of the Secretary-General at the seventy-ninth session of the General Assembly, in 2024. The Office remains confident that the project implementation schedules will be on track and within the approved budget. The United Nations Office at Geneva is preparing the Secretary-General’s eleventh annual progress report on the strategic heritage plan and is confident that it will show a projected year-end unspent balance that is substantially lower than the previous year’s balance. This report will also include an updated project schedule and overall cost plan, reflecting the ongoing efforts to enhance scheduling and cost forecasting.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration improve the formulation of resource requirements for multi-year capital construction budgets based on actual project implementation and revised project schedules in order to limit the unspent balances of the projects at the end of each budget period.
history.administration_response: Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget: The Administration considers the recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure, given that the unused balance of major capital projects has decreased in recent years. In addition, in the memorandum to all project owners on the preparation of the 2026 annual progress report, measures were taken to emphasize to the project team the need to continue to improve the accuracy of the projected resource requirements of these projects. United Nations Office at Nairobi: As at the end of 2024, the project for the replacement of office blocks A to J had a cash (allotment) balance of $11 million in the construction fund (64CFA) and $10.7 million in commitments. As at 30 March 2025, an additional $3.3 million had been spent and an additional $1.8 million committed. The project is at the final stage of contract amendments in order to commit the remaining $6 million allotment balance (sect. 33) in the second quarter of 2025 and to disburse the commitments by the end of 2025, as indicated in the progress report of the Secretary-General on the replacement of office blocks A–J at the United Nations Office at Nairobi (A/79/267), following the acceptance of the final accounts for the substantial completion of the new building, scheduled for March 2025, and for the substantial completion of the flexible workspace strategies component, scheduled for December 2025.
history.board_assessment: Given that the Board has updated the recommendation on budget proposals and implementation progress for multi-year construction projects, the Board considers the recommendation to be overtaken by events.
